11wbxt: Original SpanishCue material; the situations and data are for teaching purposes, not real news or official exam texts.
qlh6c4: The minutes of a neighborhood meeting said that everyone agreed to organize a fair on Saturday. The recording showed a much less clear conversation. One person had said «bueno» after hearing the proposal; another had answered «me da igual» while asking how much it would cost; a third had tried to add a condition that got buried by a change of subject. The person in charge of the minutes interpreted the absence of an explicit rejection as general consent.
yia7gb: On reviewing the exchange, the group discovered that the markers had served different functions. The first bueno was buying time, not accepting. Me da igual referred to the day, not the budget. The interrupted contribution asked that the fair end before ten. No word was especially difficult on its own; the difficulty lay in following what each turn was responding to and what was still pending. Understanding a conversation requires reconstructing those relationships as well as recognizing vocabulary.
315y56: The next meeting adopted a simple practice: before closing an agreement, someone would rephrase it and ask whether it reflected what had been said. «Entonces, si les entiendo bien, aceptamos el sábado siempre que el presupuesto no aumente y terminemos antes de las diez». That sentence did not eliminate the differences, but it offered a clear opportunity to correct them. It was also agreed that a necessary interruption would include handing the turn back: «Perdona, necesito aclarar la cifra; después seguimos con tu propuesta».
1ik9ng7: Some people feared that these formulas would make the conversation artificial. Over time they found that it was enough to use them at decisive moments. Spontaneity does not depend on speaking without pauses or repairs. A fluent conversation allows for doubts, rephrasing, and changes of perspective without anyone losing their right to be heard. The purpose of the markers is not to decorate speech, but to help people know what is being done with each contribution.
